interest: Although this file consists only of a single 'List of Papers' docket sheet rather than the underlying despatch itself, it provides a valuable administrative trace of U.S. diplomatic and economic intelligence on Japan leading up to the Pacific War. It documents that Ambassador Joseph C. Grew submitted an analysis of Japan's gold position as of November 1, 1940, reflecting the State Department's keen interest in Japan's gold reserves and capacity to finance strategic imports amid escalating U.S. economic pressure. Furthermore, the notation provides researchers with a direct cross-reference to decimal file 894.515/70, where the full substantive report was filed.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46) filed under decimal file 894.6341 (OCR'd as 1994.5341), which covers Japanese mining, concessions, and precious metals (specifically gold). The sheet records sub-number 6, identifying Despatch No. 5168 dated November 22, 1940, from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Japan, which transmitted an analysis of Japan's gold position as of November 1, 1940, along with a cross-reference noting its filing under 894.515/70.

subfiles.summary: This document is a Department of State 'List of Papers' inventory sheet (Form DS-46) for classification 894.6341 (OCR'd as 1994.5341), covering gold and precious metals in Japan. It registers sub-entry 6, recording Despatch No. 5168 dispatched by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew from Japan on November 22, 1940. The purport notes that the despatch submitted an analysis of Japan's gold position as of November 1, 1940, and provides a cross-reference to decimal file 894.515/70.
